findings.proposedFix: Scoped stylesheet keyed on [data-ahv-route="/enquiry-form/"] [data-source-pointer^="/sections/5"]: (1) wrap each channel block (…/c/3/c/3/c/N) as a card — white bg, 1px #E0D7C4, 4px radius, 24px padding — and lay them out as a 3-col grid ≥1024px, 1-col below; (2) small DOM pass that converts the 'How'/'Expect' label text nodes into <dt>/<dd> or prefixes them with a gold 12.5px uppercase eyebrow span + spacing, so 'HowOpens' becomes 'HOW — Opens…'; (3) DOM pass that turns 'Open WhatsApp' / 'Open Instagram' / 'Open Messenger' / 'Call +91…' / 'Open chat panel' / 'Go to the form' paragraphs into <a> elements styled with the site secondary button (50px, 2px #5A4420 outline, 700 weight) using the hrefs already present on the same dataset entries; (4) style 'Recommended' / 'Fastest · Personal' etc. as eyebrow chips (12.5px uppercase gold, letter-spacing 2px); (5) testimonial blocks (…/c/7) as cards with the 5-star string rendered in gold #C1882C and a non-breaking space inserted between name <strong> and role; (6) hide the orphan 'with' node and the split 'Or call:' anchor becomes its own outline button. findings.selectorOrPointer: [data-sc-name="AHV Chrome Header"] a.scp8 / a.scp3 (BOOK NOW / BOOK YOUR STAY); footer button[data-dc-tpl="121"]

checkedAndClean: Typography family + scale matches the benchmark language on all 3 routes, both widths: body Mulish 17px (p/li 17.5px, line-height 29.75px = 1.7), h1 Marcellus 35.1px (390) / 51.2px (1280), h2 Marcellus 25px / 28.16px, h3 Marcellus 22px, weight 400, ink rgb(42,33,24). Body text is above the 17px floor everywhere (histogram: p@17.5 x13, li@17.5 x10-12, li@17 x5-7, strong@17.5; no article text below 17px).

Colour tokens: body background rgb(247,244,234) = #F7F4EA paper; ink #2A2118; links green rgb(0,96,56) = #006038; gold button rgb(238,180,30) = #EEB41E with ink text; brown rgb(90,68,32) = #5A4420. Eyebrow/TOC label uses rgb(143,98,18) (#8F6212), a darker gold than the benchmark #C1882C — measured, but it raises contrast on paper from ~2.9:1 to ~5:1 for 12-13px uppercase text, so it is not reported as a defect.
Eyebrow present above the h1 on every route (uppercase, tracked 2.4-2.6px, gold) — matches the benchmark eyebrow-over-heading pattern; size is the only issue (reported above).
No horizontal overflow: documentElement.scrollWidth == clientWidth on all 6 captures (390/390 and 1280/1280); zero elements extend past the right edge.

Desktop is a genuine desktop layout, not the phone column stretched: [data-dc-tpl="21"] is a CSS grid 284.8px + 854.4px with a 64px gap; article max-width 734.4px (= 70ch at 17.5px, inside the 45-75ch rule); TOC nav is position:sticky top:96px; h1 max-width 825.5px; footer is a 4-column grid (4 x 267.8px). Mobile collapses the TOC into a <details> with a 64px summary row and 58px-tall link rows.

Mobile line length is 35ch (367px column at 17.5px Mulish). This is below the 45ch rule but is the physical maximum at >=17px on a 390px viewport (even a 0px gutter gives ~37ch), so it is recorded here rather than as a fixable finding; desktop is 70ch.

Tap targets: 44-47 interactive elements per route on mobile; only the inline mailto link is under 44px (reported). Breadcrumb 'Home' 44x44, TOC rows 333x58, hamburger 44x44, footer contact rows 350x44, social icons in 44px circles.
Heading hierarchy has no level skips on any route (h1 > h2 > h3); exactly one h1 per page (#page-h1), article is aria-labelledby it; TOC is a labelled nav landmark; skip link present.

Section rhythm on desktop: h2 margin-top 40px / margin-bottom 14px, p margin-bottom 18px, top section padding 32/28px, content block padding 56/72px — calm and consistent across the three routes (screenshots privacy-policy-1280-band1/2.png).

Images: the two banners have rounded 4px corners matching the site language; intrinsic width/height attributes match the file aspect ratios (1440x459 vs 1200x382 both 3.14:1; 832x400 exact) so no layout shift; logos load and render (colour logo 140x33 mobile / 171x40 desktop, white footer logo 136x54 / 136x68). No broken or placeholder-looking images beyond the stock-photo concern reported above.

Links: no inline links run together in the article body (the adjacent-link pairs measured are the header nav and footer nav lists, each with 44px rows and visible gaps). Body links are green, underlined on hover.

Inline styles: ~285-306 elements carry inline style (the design-runtime output) but none fight the site language — every inline value observed uses the paper/ink/gold/brown tokens and Mulish/Marcellus. Any scoped fix must use !important or an equal-or-higher specificity because of these inline declarations.
Consent banner suppressed as instructed (localStorage ktahv-consent=accepted) — nothing overlapped the measured content in any screenshot.

findings.title: Legacy sidebar menu renders as body content above the article on 2 of 3 routes

findings.title: Same stock-looking aerial paddy-field hero reused with empty alt on all three routes; not the benchmark's full-bleed overlaid-title hero

checkedAndClean: Body typography matches the benchmark and the 45-plus floor: body 17px Mulish on paper #F7F4EA ink #2A2118, line-height 28.9px; article paragraphs/list items 17-17.5px (pHist: awards 17px x19, training 17.5px x52, alcohol-free 17.5px x19) with line-height 30.6px; no article body text under 17px except the table cells and H6 labels reported above.

Display type matches: H1 Marcellus 32-34px mobile / 46px desktop, H2 Marcellus 22-26px mobile / 29-31px desktop, H3 Marcellus 22-23px, weight 400, ink colour — same family and proportions as the homepage (h1 30 / h2 26).

Paragraph line length on desktop is within range: 72ch (awards, 755px) and 74-76ch (training, alcohol-free, max-width:76ch inline). On mobile the measured 32-35ch is below the 45ch target but is arithmetically forced by 390px minus 16px gutters at ≥17px Mulish (45ch ≈ 430px), so it is not reported as a defect.

Awards route (dataset article-family-data.js) is the template's good exemplar: gold eyebrow above H1, two-column desktop layout with a sticky 320px accordion sidebar (44-48px rows), award photos in bordered rounded cards (border #E0D7C4, radius 4px, white), Marcellus card captions — it matches the packages-page card language.

Real photography throughout the article bodies where photos exist (award badges, B/W therapy training photo 371x434 rendered 1:1 on desktop, 367x429 on mobile); no placeholder graphics; images carry border-radius 4px consistent with the site's rounded corners.
Breadcrumb and header/footer tap targets meet 44px (breadcrumb links inline-flex min-height 44px; header BOOK NOW 99x44; nav rows min-height 44px); mobile hamburger button 44x44.

Colour tokens in use are the benchmark's: links/green #006038, brown button #5A4420, gold eyebrow rgb(143,98,18)/#C1882C, table header band #F1EBDD, borders #D8CFBD/#E0D7C4 — no off-palette colours found in the article bodies.

Inline styles (260-459 per page) are the renderer's own token-consistent styles (Marcellus/Mulish, 17.5px, 76ch, 4px radius) and do not fight the site language; none introduce foreign fonts or colours.

findings.title: KTAHV banned words in this template family's copy (journey, luxury)
findings.evidence: Rendered on /book-now/ at 390 and 1280 (p, 19px, main#main-content section[data-state=direct-visit]): "Secure your adventure today and begin your journey of Ayurvedic healing and relaxation." findings.benchmarkRule: KTAHV language lock overrides the design benchmark: banned words never ship on KTAHV pages, any casing.
findings.proposedFix: Not a stylesheet fix. Flag to Abilash / content owner: the captured legacy copy for /book-now/, /emailsubscriber/ and /contact-us/thank-you/ needs a compliant rewrite in the dataset (Lane B, EN + DE/FR or flagged EN-only). Do not ship the family while these strings render.

findings.title: Live /thanks/ tells the reader it cannot confirm their enquiry while the tab says Thank you
findings.evidence: Direct visit to /thanks/ at 390 and 1280 renders H1 "Return to the website" (Marcellus 35.1px / 51.2px) and p "This page cannot confirm whether a message or booking was submitted." with document.title "Thank you — your enquiry is with our care team | Kairali Ayurvedic Healing Village". The full next-steps state (H1 "Thank you — your enquiry is with our care team", Step 01–03, "Priya is here in the meantime" card, "While you wait" cards) exists in the template but only renders when resolveReceipt() returns true — public/ahv/assets/confirmation-family-render.js:12-16 accepts only ?receipt=prototype or the private Tweaks prop ("A URL/query is NEVER treated as a submission receipt"). So every real form-redirect visitor sees the fallback.
findings.benchmarkRule: 45-plus reader must not struggle: a post-submission page that says it cannot confirm the submission, under a Thank-you title, breaks trust at the exact moment the enquiry lands.
findings.proposedFix: No CSS fix; owner decision (HARD GATE 6 governs). Either (a) wire the enquiry/consultation forms to redirect with a governed receipt signal the renderer is allowed to trust so the next-steps state shows, or (b) align the direct-visit fallback title/heading so title and H1 say the same thing. Flag in QUESTIONS.md; do not self-decide.

findings.title: Sticky header + 3-row sticky jump nav pin 25% of the phone viewport while reading the cards
findings.evidence: 390x844, scrolled to scrollY=1500: header rect top 0 / bottom 64 (position: sticky), jump nav rect top 64 / bottom 210 (position: sticky; top: 64px), pinned chrome = 210px of 844px (24.9%). The nav is a 2-column grid (grid-template-columns 175.3px 175.3px) holding 5 anchor links at min-height 48px, so it wraps to 3 rows = 146px tall. Card <li> elements carry scroll-margin-top: 230px, confirming the design already accounts for the stack. mobile-scrolled.png shows the top quarter of the screen occupied by logo/BOOK NOW/hamburger plus three rows of uppercase links above the Ayurveda Programs card. Desktop is fine: header is position: relative (scrolls away), nav pins at 52px only.
findings.benchmarkRule: Hard rule: 45-plus reader on a phone; calm section rhythm with clear separation. Benchmark home/packages pages have no secondary sticky bar stacked under the header.
findings.proposedFix: Scoped stylesheet keyed on [data-ahv-route="/knowledge-centre/"]: at max-width 767px turn the jump nav (nav[style*="position: sticky"] containing a[href^="#"], inside main section[data-dc-tpl="23"]'s sibling) into a single horizontally scrolling row — .jump > div { display:flex; flex-wrap:nowrap; overflow-x:auto; gap:0 20px; -webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch } a { white-space:nowrap; min-height:52px } — so the pinned bar is 52px, or set the nav position: static on mobile and let only the header pin. Reduce li scroll-margin-top from 230px to ~124px (64 header + 52 bar + 8) in the same rule.
